chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-'Alawi, from al-'Amraki, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who had a nosebleed, then blew his nose, and that blood became small pieces and fell into his vessel. Is wudu (ablution) from it valid? He said: “If there is nothing discernible in the water, then there is no harm. But if it is something clearly visible, then he should not perform wudu (ablution) from it.”

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with water into which small pieces of blood have fallen?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about water used for wudu (ablution) when tiny pieces of blood from a nosebleed fall into a vessel. If no trace of the blood is discernible in the water, using it is permitted; but if the blood is clearly visible, wudu (ablution) should not be performed from it.
